options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Which one starts highlighted, by index into `choices`. Defaults to 0. A separator or a disabled choice is passed over for the next one on offer.
options.name: initial

options.description: Whether the cursor wraps from one end of the list to the other. Defaults to `true`; `false` stops it at the first and last choice on offer.
options.name: loop

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: An answer to start from: the choice whose `value` this is starts highlighted, and beats `initial`. Compared the way a `Map` compares keys. A value no choice on offer holds is dropped rather than refused, and `initial` decides instead.
options.name: value

registryDescription: The six prompts: text, multiline, password, confirm, select and multiselect
